messages:
customer_jane: Hey @support — we're getting a surge of 429s from the /v1/rerank endpoint in prod starting ~11:40 UTC. Clients see HTTP 429 with body: {"error": "quota_exceeded"}. This is only for tenant `tenant-xyz` and started after a small release. Example repro (from one of our clients):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"find best docs","documents":["d1","d2",...],"top_k":10}'
```
Request rate from that client ~800 req/min during bursts. Can you advise whether this is a quota config problem or a bug?

alex_support: Thanks — sorry about the outage. Can you paste the full response headers (we especially need any x-rw-ratelimit-* headers) and a request-id from the failed response? Also which region / model variant are you calling? I can open an emergency ticket.

customer_jane: Pasting one failed response (redacted):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
x-rw-ratelimit-limit: 300
x-rw-ratelimit-remaining: 0
x-rw-ratelimit-reset: 60
x-rw-request-id: req_01Fabcd2xy
{ "error": "quota_exceeded", "message": "per-route quota exceeded" }
```
We call model `rerank-v1` in us-west-2. We've got a cron job that triggers ranking right after ingest but it wouldn't have changed recently.

alex_support: Got it — opening ticket #SUP-12345 and escalating to infra. @maria_engineering can you take a look? I'm also going to request a temporary quota bump for tenant-xyz while we investigate.

maria_engineering: Looking now. I can see the same request-id. There's a strong spike pattern: spikes every minute with ~600 small requests concentrated in 5s windows. That's exactly what a cron fanout looks like. Our per-tenant per-route token bucket limit is 300 req/min with burst size 50 by default, so bursts >50 will get 429s even if the average stays below 300.

maria_engineering: Quick mitigation options:
- Increase tenant quota/burst temporarily (we can do this immediately)
- Suggest client-side smoothing: spread requests over 60s or use randomized jitter
- Batch more items per rerank request (rank top 100 in a single call rather than 10x10)
- If acceptable, fall back to embedding-similarity as a cheaper, less-throttled path for periodic jobs

sage_infra: I applied a temporary change: tenant-xyz quota bumped to 2000 req/min and burst to 120 for 1 hour to avoid immediate customer impact. change-id: rl-change-789. Also added a short-term rule to log high-burst tenants.

deploy-bot: [infra] rl-change-789 applied to tenant-xyz (quota=2000/min, burst=120) — rollout started.

customer_jane: Thanks — after the bump 429s dropped to near-zero. We'll push a client change to smooth and batch. Can you advise the recommended production limits for this workload?

maria_engineering: For scheduled rerank pipelines we usually recommend either:
- 1 request per second (60/min) if each request is small (top_k=10), or
- batch up to top_k=100 and run ~20 requests/min, which is far cheaper and friendlier to the rate limiter.
If you need sustained high QPS, we should move tenant-xyz to a dedicated capacity plan (Redwood Dedicated) so you get predictable throughput and higher burst windows. I've noted an action to review default burst settings for rerank routes.

alex_support: I've created an internal follow-up (SUP-12345) to coordinate quota expansion and a proposals doc for rerank default limits. I've looped in sales for permanent quota increase.

customer_jane: One minor ask — can we have the rate-limit headers include per-tenant human-friendly wording or a link to the docs? The current header is terse and clients keep misinterpreting reset times.

maria_engineering: Good point — ops backlog item. We'll add a short link in the response header and a clearer message in the 429 body.

alex_support: Updating ticket -> status: triaged -> assigned to eng-rl. Will close once customer confirms smoothing rollout and no more 429s. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
